sources.title: Daron Acemoglu, MIT 14.661 — Lectures 11–13: Search, Matching and Unemployment (December 2017)
sources.use: Continuous-time CRS matching intensities, flow balance, vacancy and worker values, pair-specific Nash bargaining, entry and constrained-efficiency context. Original chapter supplies full stationary boundary and discounted planner verification, shocks, financing examples and identification critique.
sources.verification: Current author v13_b_peer inspected the actual official MIT PDF web-extracted body: cover physical page1; physical pages34–54 for continuous-time matching and pair-specific surplus; physical pages56–70 for equilibrium, dynamics and welfare/Hosios discussion. Read surrounding capital passages only to exclude their assumptions. Physical PDF page = printed slide label; document has105physical pages with slides labelled through104. Earlier accepted v06-c05-matching record inspected physical34–56; this is retained provenance, not confused with current reading. No current local PDF or equation-image inspection is claimed.
sources.limits: The source adds physical capital; our model has no capital input, reversible or irreversible. Its numerical/historical evidence, assignment-model sections and full course are not imported. The source discounted welfare discussion states a solution without our complete finite-T verification; that proof is original here. Source extracted equations have sign/index irregularities; we independently derive all value, entry and welfare expressions. No universal non-CRS inefficiency claim or real-world bargaining estimate is adopted.

runtime_boundary: Preparation record and external source bodies are provenance only, not dependencies of the four-file checker.
originality: Four original worked cases, ten original exercises/solutions, complete original stationary and discounted planner proofs. No source numerical problems or prose copied.
